unsupported_codes.reason: Internal derangement of knee, the category that holds the meniscus derangement codes: reporting one treats the meniscus tear as established, and the note gives it only as 'consistent with'.
Tear of meniscus, current injury: the same assumption, and the note records no injury.

citations.M25.561: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section IV.H: in the outpatient setting a diagnosis documented as 'consistent with', or with another term that indicates uncertainty, is not coded; the condition is coded to the highest degree of certainty for the visit, such as symptoms or signs. Section I.B.18: if a definitive diagnosis has not been established by the end of the encounter, it is appropriate to report codes for signs or symptoms in its place. Here the assessment is right knee pain, consistent with medial meniscus tear, and an MRI is ordered to look for the tear, so the knee pain is reported and the tear is not.

coder_notes: The tear is an uncertain diagnosis in an outpatient visit. The joint line tenderness and the positive McMurray test are exam findings, not diagnoses. The X-rays are normal. No injury is recorded, so there is no external cause to report.
